title: Tenant Data Classification and Onboarding Privacy Scan Playbook
author: Leah Martinez
content:
Overview
This playbook defines the standard process, automated checks, and acceptance criteria used by Customer Success and Security when onboarding an enterprise tenant to Redwood. It focuses on tenant data classification, automated privacy scanning of ingested artifacts, and remediation handoffs. The goal is to ensure that customer-sensitive data is identified, protected, and routed to the correct deployment configuration (hosted/dedicated/private) before production traffic begins.

Why this exists
- Reduce legal/compliance risk by surfacing regulated data early in onboarding.
- Provide deterministic acceptance criteria for go/no-go decisions.
- Enable automation to speed onboarding while preserving security review rigor.

Scope
This playbook applies to:
- New dedicated and private tenants, and hosted customers with regulated data commitments.
- Ingested customer artifacts during provisioning: sample payloads, prompt logs, knowledge-base uploads, schema/contract files, and telemetry samples.
- Activities performed by the Customer Success (CS) Onboarding Engineer, Security Reviewer, and the tenant's technical contact.

Definitions
- Sensitive Data: Data elements that are either regulated (PII, PHI, financial account numbers) or classified by the customer as confidential.
- Data Classification Tag: One of PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, REGULATED.
- Privacy Scan: An automated pipeline that runs pattern detection, ML-based entity recognition, and custom tenant rules against sample data.

Owner and escalation path
- Primary owner: Customer Success — Leah Martinez (Onboarding Lead).
- Security review owner: Security — Priya Nair.
- Escalation to Product Security: Security Pager and product-security@redwood.ai.
- SLA for review completion: 3 business days from initial scan results for non-blocking findings; 1 business day for blocking findings.

Prerequisites before running the playbook
1) Tenant has completed provisioning ticket with sample artifacts uploaded to the onboarding bucket.
2) Customer success has collected the tenant data classification questionnaire (see sample below).
3) Access controls: Onboarding engineer has a temporary least-privilege role to read onboarding artifacts.

Tenant data classification questionnaire (sample)
- Primary data types expected (free text): e.g., user-support transcripts, payment tokens, medical notes.
- Legal/regulatory constraints: e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS.
- Retention windows requested: e.g., 90 days, 7 years.
- Redaction/pseudonymization required before storage: yes/no.
- Allowed environments: hosted/dedicated/private.

Automated privacy scan: technical design (high level)
- Stage 1: Pattern ruleset (regex) for common identifiers (SSN, credit card PAN, email addresses, IPv4/IPv6).
- Stage 2: Named-entity recognition (NER) model trained for PII/PHI identification for free text.
- Stage 3: Schema inference for structured payloads (JSON/YAML) to detect keys that look like sensitive attributes (e.g., "ssn", "dob", "account_number").
- Stage 4: Tenant-specific allowlist/denylist application (customer-provided rules take precedence).
- Output: a JSON-formatted findings report plus an annotated sample file with inline marks for detected tokens.

Command-line example (onboarding engineer)
1) Download artifacts for tenant redwood-tenant-42:
   aws s3 sync s3://onboarding-artifacts/redwood-tenant-42 ./tenant-42-samples --profile onboarding-readonly
2) Run privacy scanner locally (container):
   docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data ghcr.io/redwood/privacy-scan:stable scan --input /data/tenant-42-samples --output /data/tenant-42-scan-report.json
3) Preview report:
   jq .summary tenant-42-scan-report.json

Sample findings report (excerpt)
{
  "summary": "2 files with REGULATED tokens, 5 files with CONFIDENTIAL tokens",
  "findings": [
    {"file": "support_transcript_20260111.txt", "tokens": ["EMAIL", "DOB"], "confidence": 0.92},
    {"file": "kb_upload_customer.json", "tokens": ["credit_card", "account_number"], "confidence": 0.97}
  ]
}

Acceptance criteria and gating rules (go/no-go)
- Block onboarding (no-go) if any of the following are detected in production-bound sample sets: unredacted PANs/credit card numbers, unredacted full SSNs, or PHI that customer requires to remain off-hosted.
- Soft findings (requires mitigation plan) include: many email addresses, hashed identifiers that are reversible, or aggregated personal profiles without explicit consent.
- If REGULATED tokens are found and the customer requested hosted deployment, shift to dedicated/private or implement approved tokenization workflow before go-live.

Mitigation patterns and recommended remediations
- Redaction: Replace token values with deterministic placeholders. (Example: replace PAN except last 4 digits.)
- Pseudonymization: Apply one-way hashing with tenant-scoped salt; document salt custody.
- Tokenization: Recommend Redwood Token Service (RTS) integration for high-risk tokens.
- Field-level encryption: For private/dedicated tenants, recommend KMS-managed field encryption.
- Data minimization: Reduce sample size and remove long-lived transcripts from production ingestion.

Owner handoff templates (checklist)
1) CS confirms scan report and marks each finding with severity (blocker/major/minor).
2) Security reviews and signs off (security@redwood.ai) or requests changes.
3) Engineering runs any required ingest-side transformations (redaction/pseudonymization).
4) CS validates updated sample artifacts and re-runs the scanner.
5) Final signoff recorded in onboarding ticket and QBR readiness checklist.

Operational runbook: day-of-provision checklist (numbered)
1) Verify tenant metadata in the provisioning system (tenant ID, region, allowed deployment modes).
2) Confirm sample artifacts present and decrypt if needed using onboarding key.
3) Run privacy scan and attach report to ticketing system.
4) Triage findings with customer technical contact and create mitigation tasks.
5) If blocker found, pause cutover and open a security review; notify stakeholder list (CS, Security, Engineering, Legal).
6) After mitigation, run a smoke test ingest with a modified telemetry stream and validate no blocking tokens are present.

Table: Data Classification Matrix (text representation)
- PUBLIC    | Example: marketing copy, public changelog | Storage: default | Controls: none
- INTERNAL  | Example: internal logs without identifiers   | Storage: internal | Controls: RBAC, 90d retention
- CONFIDENTIAL | Example: customer business metrics, user IDs | Storage: encrypted | Controls: field encryption, access audit
- REGULATED | Example: PHI, PAN, SSN                      | Storage: dedicated/private recommended | Controls: tokenization, KMS/HSM, legal review

Alerting and metrics
- Key telemetry emitted by the scanner: findings_count, regulated_tokens_count, scan_duration_seconds.
- CS dashboard thresholds: regulated_tokens_count > 0 triggers immediate security review.
- Sample SLOs for the pipeline: 99% of scans complete within 30 minutes for datasets <= 100MB.

Common false positives and tuning guidance
- Regex collisions: long alphanumeric IDs may look like PANs; tune regex to require known separators and checksum rules where possible.
- Locale-specific dates/numbers: avoid flagging common date formats as DOB unless adjacent tokens indicate a person.
- Customer-specific labels: load tenant allowlist early (tenant.rules.allowlist) to reduce noise.

Audit evidence and QBR artifacts
- Store final signed scan report in the onboarding ticket and in the tenant evidence archive (S3 path recorded in ticket).
- QBR checklist item: evidence that either no REGULATED tokens were present or that an approved mitigation was implemented.

Frequently asked questions (short)
Q: What if the customer refuses to remove sample data containing regulated tokens?
A: For hosted deployments, this is a block. Offer a dedicated/private deployment path or an RTS tokenization integration. Document the decision and obtain an executive escalation if required.

Q: Can the scanner be run on live traffic?
A: Not by default. Live traffic scanning must be explicitly authorized and staged via a non-production mirror to avoid capturing production secrets in onboarding storage.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Sample tenant.rules.allowlist (YAML):
  allowlist:
    - key_regex: '^metadata\\..*$'
    - value_regex: '^(redwood-safe|demo)$'

- Appendix B: Example regex for PAN (simplified):
  (?:(?:4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?)|(?:5[1-5][0-9]{14})|(?:3[47][0-9]{13}))
